newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU unlikely to agree on beef labels on Monday.
newsitem.headline: EU unlikely to agree on beef labels on Monday.

text.p: European Union farm ministers will on Monday make further progress on proposals to identify and register cattle and to label beef, but are unlikely to reach agreement, EU diplomats said on Thursday.
Technical problems remain to be resolved and the European Parliament has not yet given an opinion on the proposed measures, they said.

In addition, EU Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler's plans to depart for Strasbourg early on Tuesday means that there will be not enough time for the Dutch EU Presidency to prepare a compromise text and the meeting is likely to end on Monday.
Fischler is attending a weekly meeting of EU Commissioners and a European Parliament debate on a report on the mad cow crisis.

On cattle registration and identification, diplomats said there were problems concerning financing, tagging and deadlines for transmitting data. Some countries also say that the planned start-up in January, 1998, is unrealistic.
On beef labelling, six member states, including Germany and France, oppose the Commission's proposal for a voluntary system.
Diplomats said a possible compromise would be to review the situation in two years time with a commitment to move towards a compulsory system.
There is also disagrement over whether the label should include the country or region of birth as well as information on fattening and slaughtering.
